GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The remediation treats the clean structural GRACE report as necessary but insufficient. Runtime regressions and stale semantic projections demonstrate that repository-owned checks must validate expected coverage, truthful dependency edges, and executable defaults rather than relying only on XML grammar and the presence of test files.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keeping Guardian under only M-CLI-COMMANDS was rejected because the broad verification entry already overclaimed coverage while omitting the command's numeric parsing and write behavior.
Changing grace-cli to require every source file was rejected because grace-cli is external to this repository and raw prompt or declaration files need explicit project-owned exceptions.
Adding GRACE comments to workflow/system-instruction.md was rejected because the file is copied into dist and injected into model context as runtime content.
Retrofitting stronger baseline assertions into archived plans was rejected because archived lifecycle artifacts are immutable historical evidence rather than current policy documents.
Keeping multiple LAST_CHANGE lines as a local changelog was rejected because grace file navigation currently surfaces only one physical entry and frequently reports an obsolete change.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Whether grace-cli should eventually gain native expected-governed-file coverage and multi-entry change-history support may be proposed upstream after the repository-owned checks prove the desired contract.
Other broad CLI commands may receive dedicated M-CLI-* modules later if future evidence shows similarly nontrivial behavior hidden behind M-CLI-COMMANDS.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user runs guardian config with timeout-ms 0.4, 1.5, zero, a negative value, or non-numeric text; the command fails without printing or writing schema-invalid config.
OpenCode invokes web_search with only query; execute requests permission and sends count eight to the selected provider.
A source edit accidentally saves hashline read prefixes around semantic headers or adds a second LAST_CHANGE; the repository check fails before commit and identifies the file.
An agent asks for workflow architecture; graph navigation reports state-to-transition and persistence-to-state dependencies consistent with source contracts and imports.

An agent investigates Web Tools product intent; requirements, graph flows, module records, and critical verification expose the canonical search and fetch behavior without consulting archived implementation plans.
A future plan changes existing behavior; its baseline uses content assertions or records an explicit rationale for an existence-only baseline before execution approval.
